title: Apostol: the Epistle cycle after Pentecost
scope: The Epistle of every day from the Tuesday after Pentecost to the Saturday before the Publican and the Pharisee, keyed by week after Pentecost (week N ends with the Nth Sunday; week 1 is Pentecost week) and day.
licence: Released with bible-rs under the MIT licence. The table holds Scripture references only: no Bible text and no prose from the sources. Notes are our own.
usage: Byzantine usage, Revised Julian fixed feasts, Julian Paschalion, in two usages: Greek (the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America as goarch.org prints it; the default) and Antiochian (the Antiochian Orthodox Christian Archdiocese of North America's service texts and charts). Where they differ both are recorded: a reading or an entry marked "in": "greek" or "antiochian" is read only in that usage, and an entry's "greek" or "antiochian" object changes its name, its rules (weekday, sunday, saturday, bright; none = no reading) or its confidence there. Slavic (OCA) and other alternatives (a patron's readings) are kept in 'variants' and 'slavic' and are never read.
numbering: English Bible (KJV/Hebrew) chapter and verse, the grid's numbering, with half-verse letters dropped. Each string in refs is one contiguous range ('Book C:V', 'Book C:V-V' or 'Book C:V-C:V', with the grid's book abbreviations); a reading's refs are read together, in order, as one lesson.
confidence: high: a source of the usage (the Antiochian service texts and charts; goarch.org) agrees with at least one independent source. medium: the sources differ (usually by a verse at the start or end) or the reference rests on one source. low: no Antiochian or Greek source was found, or the yearly ordo decides.

sources.HAP: Isabel F. Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic (Greco-Russian) Church, 1906 (public domain; archive.org cu31924029363128): tables of Epistles and Gospels.
sources.SCR: F. H. Scrivener, A Plain Introduction to the Criticism of the New Testament, Cambridge 1861 (public domain; archive.org plainintroductio00scri): Synaxarion and Menologion of the Byzantine lectionary manuscripts.

sources.WIKI: Wikipedia, articles on the Triodion and Holy Week (for Holy Week Old Testament readings only).

rules: Monday to Friday read through Romans to Jude; Saturdays and Sundays have their own series.
The Epistle never jumps: the week is always counted from Pentecost.

P, the Publican's number counted from Pentecost, is 33, 34, 37 or 38. Weeks 1-32 are read in order; later weeks count back from the Publican: week w reads week 33 - (P - w). Week 33 is always the six days before the Publican.
Sundays up to the Forefathers take their own number. From Theophany to the Triodion the Sunday Epistle follows the Gospel read: the Nth of Luke takes Sunday N+17, the Nth of Matthew Sunday N.
The Antiochian Archdiocese keeps the 2nd Sunday as All Saints of Antioch (Acts 11:19-30); Greek usage reads the cycle Epistle Rom 2:10-16.

readings.note: Sunday of All Saints of Antioch (and of North America)
The cycle Epistle of the 2nd Sunday: goarch.org 2018-2027, OCA, the 1853 index, Hapgood 1906; Antiochian service text 2023.

entries.note: Greek usage reads the cycle Epistle Rom 2:10-16. Antiochian usage: since 2025 the Archdiocese keeps the 2nd Sunday after Pentecost as the Sunday of All Saints of Antioch and of North America, reading Acts 11:19-30 in place of the cycle Epistle Rom 2:10-16. Only two years agree: the service texts read Rom 2:10-16 in 2018-2023 (in 2024 St Kyriaki, 7 July, took the day), and the 2019-2025 charts print Rom 2:10-16, even in 2025 when the service text read Acts 11:19-30; the 2026 chart and service text agree. For earlier years, and where the Antiochian commemoration is not kept, read Rom 2:10-16.
